title: The Belly and the Members
summary: In ancient days, the different parts of the human body held a bitter council of rebellion against the Belly. Through unexpected trial and turning point, each character learns that all members of a community must work together; none can survive without the quiet labor of the whole.
full_text: In ancient days, the different parts of the human body held a bitter council of rebellion against the Belly. The Hands, the Feet, the Legs, and the Mouth complained bitterly of their daily toil: "Look at the injustice of our condition!" protested the Hands. "We chop wood, dig ditches, and prepare food. The Feet walk miles carrying the whole burden, and the Teeth grind every bite. Yet the idle, lazy Belly sits comfortably in the middle, doing no work at all, consuming all the fruit of our hard labor! We shall strike against this tyrant!" They entered into a solemn covenant: the Hands swore never to carry food to the lips; the Mouth swore never to open; and the Teeth swore never to chew. For the first day, the rebellious members rejoiced in their idle freedom. But by the second day, a heavy languor fell upon them. By the third day, the Legs could no longer support the body; the Hands grew too weak to lift a feather; the Mouth was parched with burning dryness; and the Eyes sank dull into their sockets. In their fainting weakness, the members realized their grave mistake: they understood that the Belly, though silent and seemingly passive, was constantly working to digest the food and distribute strength, vitality, and blood to every limb and organ of the body. Abandoning their foolish strike, they resumed their harmonious cooperation, learning that in every society, mutual interdependence and quiet service sustain the life of the whole.
moral: All members of a community must work together; none can survive without the quiet labor of the whole.

quiz.question: In the fable "The Belly and the Members", what situation triggers the main conflict?
options: A confrontation arising from conflicting desires, needs, or natural traits
A sudden storm that drove all animals far across the open plains
A royal decree ordering all beasts to leave the countryside
A festival where the creatures exchanged gifts in harmony
quiz.hint: Recall the events that begin the story.

quiz.question: What critical action or realization changes the course of the story?
options: One character's true nature or limits are revealed through their actions
An outside judge arrives to solve the problem for both parties
Both characters agree to forget what happened and walk away
The smaller character suddenly transforms into a giant beast
quiz.hint: Think about how the conflict reaches its resolution.

quiz.question: What essential truth does "The Belly and the Members" teach young readers?
options: All members of a community must work together; none can survive without the quiet labor of the whole.
Might and physical strength always triumph over truth and wisdom
Flattery is the safest and most honest way to make lifelong friends
It is wise to pretend to be someone you are not in times of trouble
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the final moral lesson of the fable.

discussion_questions.prompt: Who are the central characters in "The Belly and the Members", and what was each trying to accomplish at the beginning?

Why does this fable conclude with the moral that "All members of a community must work together; none can survive without the quiet labor of the whole"? How do the characters' choices illustrate this?
Think of a situation at school, sports, or home where someone might face a similar dilemma. How can you apply this lesson?
Were the consequences faced by the characters fair? What alternative choice could have produced a wiser outcome?
Imagine if the characters met again one year later. How would their behavior change based on what they learned today?
